clue.text: Show reluctance being almost completely shy

indicators.note: almost completely means the synonym loses just its final letter

parts.note: shy, as in modest and reserved, means demure

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates because they are nearly always bashful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost completely' drops the final E of DEMURE.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise an objection or hesitate is to show unwillingness; the verb means exactly that.

clue.text: Consider having leaders of dastardly exploit set free

indicators.note: leaders of means the first letters of the following words

parts.note: to liberate is to set free

explanation.surface: Someone ponders freeing the instigators of a wicked scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberate is to think carefully about something.

clue.text: Virility shown by male (bill with his Maureen)

parts.note: AC, account, is a bill
Mo is a short form of Maureen

explanation.surface: A man named Bill shows off his manliness with Maureen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like a man's name; it is an account, AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Machismo is aggressive manliness, a show of masculine strength.

clue.text: Became conscious of the fact that dealer is crooked

indicators.note: crooked means bent or twisted, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone realised that a dealer was dishonest.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to become aware of it.

clue.text: Huge American soldier, good worker in charge

parts.note: GI is the usual term for a US soldier
the ant is the crossword's standard worker insect

explanation.surface: A big US serviceman described as a capable, responsible worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something enormous or colossal is huge.

clue.text: Artist has year in Indian state

indicators.note: in tells us the year letter goes inside the state

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast

explanation.surface: A painter spends a year living in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was a celebrated Spanish painter.

clue.text: Man upset by some disorder — flatulence?

indicators.note: upset says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A man is troubled by a digestive complaint involving wind.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns the run DERFLA from 'disorder flatulence' upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred is a man's name, so it can stand for a man.

clue.text: Sailor needs to obtain required standard

parts.note: tar is an old term for a sailor
to get is to obtain

explanation.surface: A seaman must reach the expected level.
explanation.definitionFit: A target is a level one aims to reach, the standard demanded.

clue.text: Fool in Conservative set

parts.note: a lot is a set or group of things

explanation.surface: An idiot among a group of Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: Clot is British slang for a stupid person.

clue.text: Be unable to find a space in the diary, alas

parts.note: to lack something is to be without it, unable to find it
a diary is divided into days, each one a space

explanation.surface: A busy person laments that their diary has no free slot.
explanation.walkthrough: LACKADAY is an old-fashioned exclamation of regret.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are archaic cries of sorrow or regret, so one can stand for the other.

clue.text: Sudden terror brought by a loud female? Absolutely!

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
right! is an emphatic reply meaning absolutely, quite so

explanation.surface: A noisy woman gives someone a real shock, and they agree emphatically.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic noun for a fright or sudden fear, the same as terror.

clue.text: Using the toilet to dispose of port

definitions.text: Using the toilet to dispose of

explanation.surface: Someone gets rid of something down the lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: Flushing is the English name of Vlissingen, a port in the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending something away with a rush of water from the cistern; also a Dutch seaport.

clue.text: Landlord's agent gets hit — trouble getting in

indicators.note: getting in tells us one piece goes inside another

parts.note: biff is informal for a hit or punch
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A rent collector is struck while forcing entry into a property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' reads as a noun in the surface but works as the verb, to afflict.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailiff acts for a landlord, collecting rent or seizing goods.

clue.text: Emergency action to make tree steady

parts.note: the fir is an evergreen tree
staid means sober and steady

explanation.surface: Instructions to support a young tree so it stays upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediate treatment given to an injured person before medical help arrives.

clue.text: One chaste lady taken out and completely overwhelmed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a nun takes a vow of chastity
someone taken out on a romantic outing has been dated

explanation.surface: A virtuous woman is courted on a date and finds it all too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Flooded with something, figuratively swamped, as with letters or work.

clue.text: Unhappy with girl's subject matter

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, so girl's is Di's
content is the subject matter of a book or talk

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes what a young woman writes about.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means dissatisfied, not happy with things.

clue.text: Very ancient, so sad ill health's getting worse

indicators.note: getting worse suggests the letters deteriorate into a new order

parts.note: the S of the possessive is needed as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone laments their declining health with old age.
explanation.walkthrough: The S in health's counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for extremely old, as old as the landscape itself.

clue.text: Fellow is sitting in shed — not one saying prayers?

indicators.note: sitting in tells us the pieces sit inside the shed

parts.note: a hut is a small shed
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A man sits alone in his shed, apparently not a churchgoer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: a humanist rejects religion, so would not pray.
explanation.definitionFit: A humanist holds non-religious views, relying on reason rather than faith or worship.

clue.text: Mild Anne can turn out to be explosive

indicators.note: can turn out suggests the letters may be turned into a new form

explanation.surface: A gentle woman named Anne may prove to have a fiery temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A buried bomb is an explosive device, explosive here used as a noun.

clue.text: Provide hospitality for volunteers at home — go in first

indicators.note: first says the piece for go in leads the others

parts.note: to enter is to go in
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: Instructions for welcoming volunteer guests at the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is the UK's reserve force of volunteer soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To host and look after guests is to give them hospitality.

clue.text: Time to get support for a plant

parts.note: an easel is a stand that supports a painting

explanation.surface: A gardener says it is time to stake a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The teasel is a prickly plant whose heads were used to raise the nap on cloth.

clue.text: Empire-builder providing highways, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word for highways is spoken, giving a word with that sound

parts.note: roads are highways

explanation.surface: An imperialist building roads across a continent.
explanation.walkthrough: Cecil Rhodes built a British empire in southern Africa; Rhodesia was named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecil Rhodes was a colonialist who expanded British rule in Africa.

clue.text: Cheer up tot in the valley

indicators.note: in tells us the summing word is placed inside the valley word

parts.note: a glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland
to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: A small child is happy down in the valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a small child; it is the verb, to tot up.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone happier or brighten their mood.

clue.text: Suit with expensive accessories

explanation.surface: Someone describes a smart outfit worn with costly jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four card suits, and also precious gems worn as jewellery.

clue.text: Instrument with only one note — odd!

parts.note: D is one of the notes of the musical scale
rum is old British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A strange instrument that can play just a single pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface jokes that a drum has only one note, but D is the note and RUM means odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum is a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Chopin's companion could be seen at the seaside

definitions.text: could be seen at the seaside

explanation.surface: The composer's partner is spotted on a beach.
explanation.walkthrough: George Sand, the French novelist, was Chopin's lover.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer George Sand was Chopin's partner, and grains on a beach are found by the sea.

clue.text: Trickery from fat Eric somehow taking one in

indicators.note: taking, with in, means one piece takes another inside it
somehow signals the letters are put together in some new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A large man named Eric is somehow pulling a fast one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fat' looks like a description of Eric, but both words are just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Artifice is clever deception or cunning, i.e. trickery.

clue.text: Man following animals gets annoyed

indicators.note: following says the man piece comes after the animals piece

parts.note: moles are burrowing animals
Ted is a man's name

explanation.surface: A gardener chasing burrowing pests becomes irritated.
explanation.definitionFit: To be pestered or harassed, the old sense of bothered.

clue.text: Turkey to consume in special celebration?

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey
to eat is to consume

explanation.surface: A Christmas turkey to be eaten at a festive meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A treat is a special outing or indulgence, an occasion of pleasure.
